text:
### Observed differences

- A06 became far more frequent and earlier: it appears in about 24 in 100 traces in the earlier window (mean relative position about 0.50, i.e. mid-trace) versus about 73 in 100 in the later window, where it sits much earlier (mean about 0.25; the upper quartile falls from about 0.91 to 0.26). [POS001, DIR001]
- A06's routing collapsed onto a single successor: before, its outgoing transitions were spread over many activities (A15 about 21 in 100, A47 about 15, A45 about 13, A16 about 8); in the later window about 88 in 100 go to A16, and A16 follows A06 within one step in about 97 in 100 of the observed pairs (about 18 in 100 before, on few observations). [DIR001, LAG002]
- A group of activities that previously ran only in about half of the cases now runs in nearly all: A14, A15 and A16 co-occur with A19, A20, A25, A26 and A41 in about 47–48 in 100 traces before versus about 995 in 1000 after; traces containing none of A19/A20/A25 together fell from about 52 in 100 to almost none. [REL009, REL012, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL022]
- A06 moved from outsider to embedded member of this group: before, it co-occurred with A14/A15/A16/A26/A41 in only about 24 in 100 traces (and with A19/A20/A25 in about 13 in 100); in the later window the share is about 73 in 100 for all of them. [REL001, REL002, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008]
- A fixed order emerged around A06: A14 precedes A06 in about 69 in 100 later cases (about 22 in 100 before), and A06 precedes A16, A19, A20, A25, A26 and A41 in about 65 in 100 cases each, where before the two orders were balanced or the pair rarely met. [REL001, REL003, REL004, REL007, REL008]
- The tail of the block became a strict sequence: A41 is followed by A19 within one step in about 98 in 100 cases, by A25 within two (about 96), by A20 within three (about 95) and by A26 within four (about 93); accordingly A19 precedes A25/A20/A26, A25 precedes A20/A26, and A20 precedes A26 in about 97–99 in 100 cases. Before, A41's exits split between A19 (about 37 in 100) and a direct A26 (about 45 in 100), and A41→A26 occurred at lag 1 almost as often as at lag 4. [DIR006, LAG018, LAG019, LAG020, LAG021, REL018, REL020, REL022, REL023, REL025]
- A15 now leads to A06 in about 40 in 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 1 in 100 before) while A15→A16 fell from about 94 to about 58 in 100; A15 and A16 also interleave or repeat more often relative to A19/A20/A25 (about 42 in 100 versus about 18 in 100). The chain A19→A25→A20 itself already dominated before (about 93–96 in 100) but only ran in about half of the traces. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL012, REL015]
- The remaining qualified items show only small shifts consistent with the same block: A14 routes to A15 in about 97 in 100 (about 85 before), A26 sits slightly later in the trace, and the A44/A46 profiles are nearly unchanged. [DIR002, DIR007, DIR008, POS002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, almost every execution runs a fixed sequence of activities — A14 and A15, then A06, then A16, and a few steps later A41 followed by A19, then A25, then A20, then A26 — whereas in the earlier window this group ran together in only about 47–48 in 100 cases with looser ordering, and A06 was a rare, mid-trace step with many different successors. In short, the block became part of nearly every execution in a set order, and A06 became a regular early step within it, leading to A16 in about 88 in 100 of its transitions. [REL009, REL012, REL018, DIR001, DIR006, LAG002, LAG018, LAG020, LAG021]

The screening produced 57 qualifying items against fewer than 1 expected without change, so chance cannot account for the set as a whole. The hypothesis is shown directly by relational evidence (co-occurrence of the block rising from about 47 to about 995 in 1000; A06's co-occurrence rising from about 13–24 to about 73 in 100), by successor changes (A06→A16 and A41→A19 becoming dominant while a direct A41→A26 disappears), and by lags establishing the one-step chain A41→A19→A25→A20→A26. Because the routing at A06 and A41 changed within the block, the difference is not merely that an existing path was taken more often. [DIR001, DIR006, LAG018, LAG021, REL009, REL018]

Limitations: many items describe the same underlying block behaviour and are not independent confirmations; positions and lags are event positions, not clock times, so no timing claim is made; and the evidence cannot fully rule out that the windows sampled a shifted mix of pre-existing case types rather than a modified control flow, although the within-block routing changes argue against a pure mix shift. A06 is still absent in about 27 in 100 later traces, so its role in those cases remains unobserved. [REL001, POS001, DIR001]

Other differences: minor concentration and position shifts (A14→A15 more dominant; A26 slightly later; small lag redistributions around A44/A46 and A16 self-repetitions) that are consistent with the same block behaviour rather than separate changes. [DIR002, DIR007, DIR008, POS002, LAG015]
